findings.issue_text: Reorder of `.extra-info-wrapper` and title relies on implicit DOM order assumption; `.title` has no explicit `order(1)`, making the layout fragile to future template changes
Legacy flexbox prefixes (2009-spec box properties) don't support `margin-left: auto` alignment or the ordering model used, giving false compatibility and broken header layout in old browsers
`.title` no longer wraps under flex; long titles lack `min-width: 0`/shrink guards and will squeeze or overflow the panel instead of wrapping
`.valign-helper` is dead weight but remains a flex item that can offset title/panel alignment; should be removed
`-ms-align-items` is a nonexistent property (IE used `-ms-flex-align`), indicating unverified vendor-prefix set
`.small-action` padding change removes avatar compensation unconditionally, degrading layout for avatar-less small-actions (no left gutter or vertical padding)
Invalid/unrecognized vendor property `-ms-align-items` in the align-items mixin (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`); the stray line is dead code copied from an old mixin set without verification

Old-spec flexbox values (`-webkit-box-align`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) use different value vocabularies (e.g., `start`/`end` vs `flex-start`/`flex-end`) and 1-based ordinal groups, so modern values like `center`, `baseline`, `3` passed to the mixin can cause misaligned or misordered layouts in old-spec browsers

align-items mixin in mixins.scss:105-113 emits invalid property -ms-align-items, and order mixin emits -moz-box-ordinal-group/-webkit-box-ordinal-group, adding dead declarations that inflate compiled CSS size

header.scss:16-18 and topic-post.scss:263-265 insert legacy prefixed display: -webkit-box/-moz-box values first, causing older-Webkit browsers to use the 2009-spec flexbox model while align-items/order use the modern spec, a correctness/compat risk
Flex children in .contents header lack flex: 0 0 auto / min-width: 0, so panel controls (hamburger, search, login) can be squished by long titles on narrow viewports due to default flex-shrink: 1
margin-left: auto for right alignment is a no-op in the old-flexbox prefixes the mixins emit (-webkit-box, -ms-flexbox), so .panel loses right alignment on those browsers
align-items() mixin emits modern values like flex-start/flex-end into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align which don't accept them, causing silent no-alignment in prefixed branches
align-items() emits the invalid property -ms-align-items, and the prefix stack is inconsistent (missing -moz-box-align; -moz-inline-box/-webkit-inline-box not real values)
Removed padding/margin on .small-action-desc and its p collapses vertical spacing for small-actions rendered without an avatar, causing collision with surrounding posts
Removed indent plus align-items: center changes multi-line clipping behavior of .small-action-desc for long titles
Making .contents a flex container invalidates remaining float children (plugin/theme float styling on .extra-info-wrapper or .panel), causing unpredictable rendering, with overlap in old WebKit
Order values leave .title at implicit 0 while .panel and .extra-info-wrapper get 2 and 3, making layout dependent on DOM-order coincidence and computing a different order in old -webkit-box spec

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reorder of `.extra-info-wrapper` and title relies on implicit DOM order assumption; `.title` has no explicit `order(1)`, making the layout fragile to future template changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit flexbox ordering in a couple places (e.g., `.panel { @include order(3); }` in `header.scss` and `.extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }` in `topic.scss`) while other siblings like `.title` no longer have an explicit positioning rule (its `float: left` was removed and no `order(...)` was added). In a flex container, unspecified `order` defaults to 0, so the visual order will implicitly follow DOM order for those items, making the layout more sensitive to future template/DOM rearrangements. This is a maintainability/fragility concern rather than a verifiable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy flexbox prefixes (2009-spec box properties) don't support `margin-left: auto` alignment or the ordering model used, giving false compatibility and broken header layout in old browsers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds legacy 2009-spec flexbox fallbacks via `@mixin flexbox()` (`display: -webkit-box; -moz-box;`) and `@mixin order()` (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) while also relying on modern flex behavior for alignment in `header.scss` (e.g., `.panel { margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }` after removing floats). In 2009-spec box layouts, `margin-left: auto` is not a reliable/right-alignment mechanism the way it is in modern flexbox, so when the legacy `display: -webkit-box` path is used, the header panel may no longer align to the right, creating a broken layout specifically in those older engines despite the presence of prefixes suggesting compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.title` no longer wraps under flex; long titles lack `min-width: 0`/shrink guards and will squeeze or overflow the panel instead of wrapping

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.contents` in `header.scss` from a non-flex layout (with `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }`) to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and removes the `.title` float entirely, while `.panel` becomes a flex item (`margin-left: auto; @include order(3);`). In flex layouts, long text in a flex item can fail to shrink/wrap as expected unless `min-width: 0` / shrink rules are set on the flex item. The diff does not add any such guard for the title element, so the concern is plausible and directly tied to this change, but the actual overflow/wrapping behavior cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone (HTML structure/other CSS not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.valign-helper` is dead weight but remains a flex item that can offset title/panel alignment; should be removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` in `header.scss` became a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), but it does not show what `.valign-helper` does, whether it is unused (“dead weight”), or even whether it is a direct child flex item. Without the relevant `.valign-helper` styles/markup context, the claim that it offsets title/panel alignment and should be removed isn’t verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `-ms-align-items` is a nonexistent property (IE used `-ms-flex-align`), indicating unverified vendor-prefix set
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that `-ms-align-items` is nonexistent and that IE used `-ms-flex-align`, which is exactly the golden issue about the incorrect legacy property for IE/Edge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.small-action` padding change removes avatar compensation unconditionally, degrading layout for avatar-less small-actions (no left gutter or vertical padding)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;` while also making `.small-action` a flex container. This unconditionally removes the previous large left padding that likely acted as a gutter/compensation for avatar positioning. However, the claim that this specifically degrades “avatar-less small-actions” cannot be verified from the diff alone (no markup/variants shown), so it’s a concrete layout-risk to check rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid/unrecognized vendor property `-ms-align-items` in the align-items mixin (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`); the stray line is dead code copied from an old mixin set without verification

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that includes both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The latter is not a recognized MS flexbox property (the MS-prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`), so it is effectively dead/ignored CSS. This doesn’t clearly break behavior (unknown properties are typically ignored), but it is a real, diff-grounded correctness/maintenance issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Old-spec flexbox values (`-webkit-box-align`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) use different value vocabularies (e.g., `start`/`end` vs `flex-start`/`flex-end`) and 1-based ordinal groups, so modern values like `center`, `baseline`, `3` passed to the mixin can cause misaligned or misordered layouts in old-spec browsers

align-items mixin in mixins.scss:105-113 emits invalid property -ms-align-items, and order mixin emits -moz-box-ordinal-group/-webkit-box-ordinal-group, adding dead declarations that inflate compiled CSS size

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that includes `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (mixins.scss), which is not a recognized MS flexbox property (IE uses `-ms-flex-align`). This will compile to a no-op/invalid declaration. The `order($val)` mixin also adds legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` declarations; whether they are truly “dead” depends on supported browsers, but they do increase output size. These are concrete, diff-grounded quality/perf concerns rather than a behavioral defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss:16-18 and topic-post.scss:263-265 insert legacy prefixed display: -webkit-box/-moz-box values first, causing older-Webkit browsers to use the 2009-spec flexbox model while align-items/order use the modern spec, a correctness/compat risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin flexbox()` which intentionally lists legacy `display: -webkit-box/-moz-box` before modern `display: flex`, but the accompanying mixins for alignment and ordering also include the corresponding legacy properties (`-webkit-box-align` in `@mixin align-items` and `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` in `@mixin order`). So it’s not true that older WebKit would be forced into the 2009 flexbox model while only modern `align-items/order` are used; the diff explicitly provides both legacy and modern properties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flex children in .contents header lack flex: 0 0 auto / min-width: 0, so panel controls (hamburger, search, login) can be squished by long titles on narrow viewports due to default flex-shrink: 1

adjudication.rationale: The diff converts `.contents` in `header.scss` into a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and makes `.panel` a flex item (`margin-left: auto; @include order(3);`) but does not set any `flex`/`flex-shrink`/`min-width` constraints on the children. Under default flexbox sizing (`flex: 0 1 auto` with `min-width: auto`), long title/content can affect how sibling items shrink/overflow on narrow viewports, potentially impacting the `.panel` controls. This risk is introduced by the switch from floats to flex without additional sizing rules, though the exact impact can’t be fully confirmed from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: margin-left: auto for right alignment is a no-op in the old-flexbox prefixes the mixins emit (-webkit-box, -ms-flexbox), so .panel loses right alignment on those browsers

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` switches from `float: right;` to `margin-left: auto;` for right alignment, while the container (`.contents`) is changed to `@include flexbox()` which emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` in addition to modern flex. Auto-margins are not part of the old `-webkit-box` box model (it relies on `-webkit-box-pack` for distribution), so on browsers that pick the legacy prefixed layout the `margin-left: auto` alignment can fail, causing `.panel` not to be right-aligned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() mixin emits modern values like flex-start/flex-end into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align which don't accept them, causing silent no-alignment in prefixed branches

adjudication.rationale: The new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` directly assigns `$alignment` to legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` (in `mixins.scss`). Those prefixed properties use older keyword sets (e.g., `start/end`) and do not accept modern `flex-start/flex-end`, so callers passing modern values would get broken alignment in prefixed branches. While this diff’s shown call sites use `center`/`baseline`, the mixin as introduced is incorrect for common `align-items` values and can silently fail when used with `flex-start`/`flex-end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() emits the invalid property -ms-align-items, and the prefix stack is inconsistent (missing -moz-box-align; -moz-inline-box/-webkit-inline-box not real values)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `@mixin align-items($alignment)` (in `mixins.scss`), the diff explicitly emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid flexbox property for the IE/Edge prefix set (the usual prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`). Also, since `@mixin flexbox()` uses the legacy `display: -moz-box;`, the corresponding legacy alignment property `-moz-box-align` is missing from `align-items()`, making the prefix stack internally inconsistent for that mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed padding/margin on .small-action-desc and its p collapses vertical spacing for small-actions rendered without an avatar, causing collision with surrounding posts

adjudication.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, and nested `p` margins are reduced from `margin: 5px 0` to `margin: 0`, with `> p` losing `padding-top: 4px`. This diff clearly removes essentially all vertical spacing for the small-action description content, which can collapse the row height and plausibly create visual overlap/tight collision with adjacent content in some renderings (e.g., when avatar-related spacing isn’t present).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed indent plus align-items: center changes multi-line clipping behavior of .small-action-desc for long titles

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action` to a flex container with `@include align-items(center)` and alters `.small-action-desc` padding/margins, but nothing here introduces/changes clipping mechanics (no fixed heights, `overflow: hidden`, or similar). The claim about “multi-line clipping behavior for long titles” is not verifiable from these SCSS changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Making .contents a flex container invalidates remaining float children (plugin/theme float styling on .extra-info-wrapper or .panel), causing unpredictable rendering, with overlap in old WebKit

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `.contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox()`), but it also removes the core floats on `.title` and `.panel` and replaces `.panel` positioning with `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`. The finding’s claim about “remaining float children” (e.g., plugin/theme float styling on `.extra-info-wrapper` or `.panel`) and “overlap in old WebKit” is not verifiable from the diff because no such remaining floated children are shown here, and the alleged plugin/theme overrides are outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Order values leave .title at implicit 0 while .panel and .extra-info-wrapper get 2 and 3, making layout dependent on DOM-order coincidence and computing a different order in old -webkit-box spec
matched_golden_ids: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that using an order/ordinal value of 0 (here, implicit for .title) behaves differently under the legacy -webkit-box ordering model, causing unintended layout differences/DOM-order dependence. This aligns with the golden issue that old -webkit/-moz box ordinal values must start at 1 and 0 leads to incorrect rendering.
